public.name: ContinuousFlexibility.Analysis.n04_referenceCurrent_transport_piece_envelope
public.header:
theorem n04_referenceCurrent_transport_piece_envelope
    (hD : IsAccumulatingProfile D) (hT : IsMaterialData D T) (hε : 0 < ε)
    (hrefState : referenceStateConditions D S C)
    (hgeom : CanonicalGeometry D S C K base ε)
    (href : CanonicalGeometry.ReferenceJets D T S C L K)
    (hcur : CanonicalGeometry.CurrentJets D T S C L K base ε)
    (z : CanonicalGeometry.Parameter S) (hz : z ∈ sectorNeighborhood S base ε ε) :
    ∃ e : ℕ → ℝ, N07aSampleSubpower T K e ∧ (∀ m, 1 ≤ e m) ∧
      ∀ m p, p ∈ referencePhysicalPieceOpen S K m →
        (∀ n : ℕ, n ≤ 2 →
          ‖iteratedFDeriv ℝ n
            (fun x => K.height (C.referenceState, 0) m x /
              K.height (liftSectorParameter S C z) m
                (canonicalCurrentPoint C K (liftSectorParameter S C z) m x)) p‖ ≤ e m) ∧
        (∀ n : ℕ, 1 ≤ n → n ≤ 2 →
          ‖iteratedFDeriv ℝ n
            (canonicalCurrentPoint C K (liftSectorParameter S C z) m) p‖ ≤ e m)
public.section_variables: {D : ReferenceData} {T : MaterialData} {S : PhysicalSpacesData} {C : NonlinearGeometryData S} {L : ReturnCorrectionData S} {K : CanonicalData S} {base : ℕ} {ε : ℝ}

mathematical_review: The positive composition estimate uses only positive outer partition lengths and positive inner block sizes for n>0. Ordered partitions and finite sum/product envelopes do not require any zero-order inverse-chart or unwrapped-angle bound.

The inverse-chart supplier is specialized to the actual geometry, ReferenceJets and CurrentJets, using their genuine chart/width bounds. Loss is chosen before n; only the fixed admissible z contributes its constant scalar factor to the sampled envelope.

The private height reciprocal helper returns both actual ContDiffOn infinity and a numerical envelope. Smoothness follows independently from H smoothness, the actual current inverse MapsTo into its moving physical piece, composition, and H positivity, then ContDiffOn.inv.

The source-factor-inverse times absolute inverse Jacobian identity cancels the actual density to H(G)^(-1). The geometry-only inverse Jacobian formula, canonicalSource definition and exact affine unit inverse identify the same point. No numerical inverse determinant lower bound is invented.

Reference charts are specialized at (C.referenceState,0) using the actual neighborhood and sector proofs. Only the reference physical domain is rewritten by referenceDomain; moving physicalPieceOpen is never equated with the fixed reference piece.

Reference height is the actual Fin6 physical field slot 2. Reference chart bounds supply the needed positive orders. The quotient bound uses the genuine product and composition envelopes, then an open EqOn congruence to the literal quotient.
Transport is identified by a full function equality G o F_ref = canonicalCurrentPoint, avoiding partial-application simplification. The quotient uses an explicit open-domain EqOn equality.

The final e is 1 plus Fin3 quotient envelopes for orders 0,1,2 plus Fin2 transport envelopes for orders 1,2. Nonnegativity, single_le_sum and n-1+1=n for positive n yield one e>=1 before all pieces, points and those orders.
All estimates preserve the same D,T,S,C,L,K, base, epsilon, fixed z and sample T.sample(K.cell m). No E0>=1 replacement, new witness, or equality between distinct half-cell samples is used.
No N04Properties or PrimitiveGeometry material/transport target is an input. The conclusion is the actual piecewise sampled envelope, not global material transport or CurrentJets construction.
